title: Four space clocks show why staying put matters as much as launching
summary: Curiosity nears 5,000 Martian days while climbing Mount Sharp, Juice borrows Earth's momentum on 28 September for Jupiter, a 222-metre lunar crater is dated to spring 2024 and a distant ring system has thinned in a decade — the lunar record is the largest yet found by modern orbiters, not proven the largest ever formed.

Primary study 'JWST occultation reveals unforeseen complexity in Chariklo's ring system' by Pablo Santos-Sanz et al. (IAA, Granada) reports near-infrared JWST stellar occultation of (10199) Chariklo: inner dense ring C1R became significantly more opaque than previous visible-light observations (replenishment/dynamical restructuring), outer ring C2R shows much weaker near-infrared signature than earlier detections (possible material loss/transient or wavelength-dependent opacity); scenarios not mutually exclusive

claims.text: Science Advances Robinson et al. abstract states 'This is the largest contemporary impact crater found in the Solar System' and introduction states 'the largest contemporary impact crater discovered anywhere in the Solar System' — qualified to instrumentally observed new craters in space-age monitoring era (LRO WAC monthly imaging since 2010), not largest crater ever formed in solar-system history. NASA feature paraphrases as 'largest, newly formed crater ever found in the solar system' without 'contemporary/discovered' qualifier.

claims.text: Frequency estimate is model-dependent: Robinson et al. crater production model predicts once every 132 years on the Moon on average; NASA feature hedges as 'about once in a century or even longer' and APOD states 'only expected once every 132 years.' Conflation of 'once-in-a-century' (100 years) and 132 years reflects uncertainty range/hedging.

claims.text: Largest fresh Martian craters discovered by MRO/HiRISE in contemporary era are smaller than McGetchin: Posiolova et al. Science 2022 reports 'Two >130-meter-diameter impact craters formed on Mars during the later half of 2021. These are the two largest fresh impact craters discovered by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter since operations started 16 years ago' including ~150-m crater on 24 Dec 2021, both smaller than McGetchin's 222 m.

sources.title: Posiolova et al. Science 2022 DOI 10.1126/science.abq7704

claims.text: Superlative should be framed as 'largest discovered/known contemporary crater' rather than largest ever formed: LRO WAC since 2010 and MRO/HiRISE since 2006 provide baseline; larger ancient craters exist, and undetected contemporary craters could exist outside monitored areas/times. ScienceAdviser paraphrase as 'Solar System's largest known impact crater to have recently formed' captures 'known/discovered' limitation.
